input: Pitch my short film idea to producers

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user needs help developing the pitch itself, the film concept, or both determines how much foundational work is required before any outreach begins.
The type of producers being targeted — indie, studio-affiliated, genre-specific — completely changes the tone, format, and content of the pitch.
Whether this is a live meeting, a film festival, a cold email, or a formal pitch event shapes the format and length of the pitch materials needed.
A hard deadline (e.g., an upcoming festival or scheduled meeting) determines urgency and how much time can be spent on preparation.
The genre, tone, and style of the film idea directly influences how the pitch should be framed and what elements to emphasise.
Understanding what the user wants from producers — funding, a co-producer, distribution, or just feedback — defines what a successful pitch outcome looks like.
Knowing what pitch materials already exist (logline, treatment, script, lookbook) determines what still needs to be created versus refined.

gold.taskTitle: Pitch Short Film Idea to Producers
gold.taskDescription: Prepare and deliver a compelling pitch for an original short film concept to attract producer interest.

questions.title: What does your short film concept focus on?
questions.description: Understand the genre, theme, and tone of the film idea — e.g., a dramatic character study, a sci-fi thriller, a comedic slice-of-life — so the pitch can be framed appropriately.

questions.title: What do you want producers to commit to or provide?
questions.description: Clarify the desired outcome of the pitch — full funding, co-production, distribution deal, or simply an expression of interest — to define what a win looks like.

questions.title: What type of producers are you pitching to?
questions.description: Identify whether the targets are independent producers, streaming platform executives, genre-specific companies, or festival-circuit producers, as this shapes tone and content.

questions.title: How will the pitch be delivered — live, written, or recorded?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a face-to-face meeting, a pitch event, a cold email submission, or a video pitch, as the format dictates length and structure of materials.

questions.title: Which pitch materials do you already have ready?
questions.description: Find out what already exists — logline, one-pager, full treatment, script draft, lookbook, mood board — to identify gaps that need to be created from scratch.

questions.title: Do you have a specific deadline or pitch opportunity coming up?
questions.description: Establish whether there is a fixed date — a scheduled meeting, festival deadline, or open submission window — to set the urgency and pace of preparation.

questions.title: Do you need help crafting the pitch or just structuring the outreach?
questions.description: Determine whether the user needs support developing the actual pitch narrative and materials, or primarily needs a plan for finding and approaching the right producers.
